evidence_levels.e2: plus real execution against production, proof committed
evidence_levels.e3: plus independently reproduced by a third party

integrations.name: LangChain

technology.name: LangChain
technology.what_it_is: The most widely used framework for composing LLM applications: chains, retrievers, agents and tools.

value.host_keeps: LangChain keeps orchestration, prompting, retrieval and whatever tracing stack you already run.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of each LLM interaction -- five signals with explicit provenance and an explicit measured / not-measured state -- without writing a measurement call per call site.
typical_use: Detect a behavioural regression that latency, cost and error rate do not show.
Answer an audit with signed records instead of log lines you assert yourself.
Produce runtime inputs to an EU AI Act dossier, which cannot be retrofitted.

entrypoint.snippet:
handler = NeoMundiCallbackHandler(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io")
answer = chain.invoke(question, config={"callbacks": [handler]})
print(handler.last_outcome.request_id)  # your correlation key

refusals: The provider reports no token count, so nothing is submitted and nothing is estimated.
Your own LLM call failed, so there is no complete interaction to measure.
The measurement API is unreachable, so the failure is reported and your chain is untouched.
Sampling excluded the run, so no socket opens and nothing is billed.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. sample_rate defaults to 1.0, so read the cost section before pointing this at a busy application.

integrations.name: Langfuse

technology.name: Langfuse
technology.what_it_is: An open-source LLM observability platform: traces, prompts, cost, sessions, datasets and evaluation scores, self-hosted or in the cloud.

evidence.reason: Two real measurements through client.trace(), each inside a real Langfuse observation, written by NeoMundiLangfuseBridge. Both served measurement_version 3.5.0 and were re-read from the NeoMundi API as persisted -- 0.06 CHF. That is only half the claim: all six scores, the five numeric signals and the categorical summary, were also re-read from the Langfuse server on both traces. See evidence/langfuse_readback_20261126.json. The bridge's `queued` means handed to the Langfuse client and nothing more, which is why a read-back from Langfuse is what settles it. Two refusals on real calls billed nothing: a valid measurement written outside any observation (not_written_no_trace), and an input that is not a NeoMundi measurement (not_written_unsupported_input).

value.host_keeps: Langfuse keeps the trace: prompt, completion, latency, cost, sessions, datasets, experiments, and the UI the developer already has open.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of the same interaction, written onto that Langfuse trace as scores -- one per signal the server declared measured -- with the NeoMundi request_id attached so the trace links to the signed record.
typical_use: See NeoMundi signals next to latency and cost on the trace you are already debugging.
Filter or chart Langfuse traces by a measured behavioural signal.
Jump from a Langfuse trace to the signed, third-party-verifiable NeoMundi record.

entrypoint.snippet:
bridge = NeoMundiLangfuseBridge(langfuse)  # your existing Langfuse client
outcome = bridge.write(trace.close())  # a neomundi TraceRecord or GovernResult
print(outcome.status, outcome.signals_written)

refusals: A signal the server did not declare measured gets no numeric score, not even its conventional value.
There is no Langfuse trace to attach to, so nothing is written.
A measurement that was not submitted writes only a summary saying so, never a signal.
A Langfuse or bridge failure is reported as an outcome and never reaches your application.

billing.note: The bridge never contacts NeoMundi and bills nothing by itself. The measurement it transports was billed when it was submitted, at 0.030 CHF per observation, by whatever produced it.

integrations.name: LiteLLM

technology.name: LiteLLM
technology.what_it_is: An LLM gateway: one OpenAI-style API to 100+ providers, as a Python library or as a proxy server, with routing, retries, budgets and logging callbacks.

evidence.route: openai-compatible endpoint (the provider publishes its usage block)

value.host_keeps: LiteLLM keeps routing, retries, fallbacks, budgets, virtual keys, its cost table and whatever logging callbacks you already run.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of every chat completion the gateway routes, to any provider, from one attachment point -- with the latency LiteLLM observed, and only token counts the provider itself published.
typical_use: Measure every provider behind a LiteLLM Proxy without instrumenting each application.
Detect a behavioural regression after a routing or model change that latency and cost do not show.
Find out, for free, which of your providers publish usage at all, with submit=False.

entrypoint.snippet:
logger = NeoMundiLogger(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io")
litellm.callbacks = [logger]
answer = litellm.completion(model="ollama_chat/llama3.2", messages=messages)

refusals: The provider published no token count; LiteLLM's zero or estimate is refused, never forwarded.
An async stream hides the provider's payload from the logger, so it is refused rather than trusted.
A cache hit, a failed call or a non-chat call is not a model interaction to measure.
The measurement API is unreachable, so the failure is reported and your call is untouched.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. sample_rate defaults to 1.0 and a gateway sees every call -- start with submit=False, which needs no key and opens no socket.

integrations.name: Microsoft Agent Framework

technology.name: Microsoft Agent Framework
technology.what_it_is: Microsoft's agent runtime, which unifies and succeeds Semantic Kernel and AutoGen -- both now in maintenance. It exposes a ChatMiddleware layer that brackets every model call, and emits OpenTelemetry natively.

evidence.reason: Nineteen offline tests, driving the framework's REAL middleware pipeline and its real OpenAI Chat Completions connector over httpx.MockTransport -- not a hand-made context. They cover a measured call, the four named refusals, four distinct failure modes including one where the measurement API itself raises, and the unit that reads the count. No real execution against the production measurement API has been performed, so no measurement_version is declared verified. qualify.py is written and its dry run was executed (free); E2 needs a separately authorised spend.

connectors_not_verified: Azure, Anthropic, Bedrock, Gemini, Mistral, Ollama
Copilot Studio, Foundry -- see LIMITATIONS section 7

value.host_keeps: Agent Framework keeps the agent runtime, the connectors, the OpenTelemetry emission, the typed usage_details and the model metadata it already carries. The middleware is added to the client and replaces nothing. And it keeps a property worth naming: when a provider publishes no token count, the framework leaves usage_details absent rather than filling it.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of each model call the framework makes -- five signals with explicit provenance and an explicit measured / not-measured state -- attached at the framework's own middleware layer, with the latency measured around the call rather than read off a span. It never invents a token count: a provider that publishes none produces a named refusal and no bill.
complements_not_replaces: otel-neomundi, which can read the same spans but must have the count declared by hand
typical_use: Measure every model call of an Agent Framework application without writing a measurement call per site.
Find out, for free and with submit=False, which of your calls could be measured at all.
Account for model behaviour to an auditor who does not take your word for it.

entrypoint.snippet:
measure = NeoMundiChatMiddleware(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io")
chat = OpenAIChatCompletionClient(model="gpt-4o-mini", middleware=[measure])
reply = await chat.get_response("What is the capital of France?")
print(measure.last_outcome.request_id)  # your correlation key

refusals: A token count is never invented. A provider that publishes none leaves usage_details absent, and the call is refused by name rather than measured.
A zero, or anything that is not a positive integer, is not a token count.

refusals.A streaming invocation is refused by nam: usage exists only once the stream is consumed, and this middleware resumes before that.

refusals: No exception of ours reaches the host application -- measured, because the framework does NOT isolate a failing middleware.

refusals.The host's own failure is recorded and r: swallowing it would hide a failure from the application.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. A refusal opens no socket and costs nothing, which examples/02_refusals.py demonstrates by printing the billed count: zero. There is no sampling in 0.1.0.

integrations.name: MLflow

technology.name: MLflow Tracing
technology.what_it_is: The tracing layer of MLflow, built on OpenTelemetry: autolog instrumentations for model clients and agent frameworks record each call as a span in a trace, stored next to the experiments and runs MLflow users already compare.

evidence.reason: Four real model calls traced by the real mlflow.openai.autolog into a throwaway local store, against Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint: two Chat Completions inside an application span, one Responses API call, and one stream with stream_options.include_usage. All four served measurement_version 3.5.0 and were re-read as persisted. Two further phases were refused on real spans and billed nothing: a stream WITHOUT include_usage (the provider published no usage, and a count is never estimated in its place) and a hand-written LLM span carrying a count the way LiteLLM's MLflow logger writes its estimate (unverified provenance). The aggregate application span is refused as an aggregate, so nothing is double-counted.

writers_verified: openai-agent (Agents SDK tracer) -- openai-agents 0.26.0 -- refused, 0/0/0 on a silent provider
langchain (mlflow.langchain.autolog) -- langchain-core 1.8.5 -- refused, copies any usage_metadata
no writer (LiteLLM's MlflowLogger) -- litellm 1.111.0 -- refused, estimate 14/7/21 on a silent provider (probe only)

value.host_keeps: MLflow keeps its autolog instrumentation, the traces, the tracking store, the UI, experiments and run comparison. The integration appends one function to MLflow's own span processors and replaces nothing.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of each model call MLflow traced, with the provider's own token count and the latency MLflow recorded -- and the NeoMundi request_id and measurement version written back on the MLflow trace, next to the run you compare.
complements_not_replaces: MLflow Tracing and its autolog integrations
the MLflow UI, experiments and evaluation
typical_use: Measure the model calls of an application MLflow already traces, without a second instrumentation.
Open an MLflow trace and find the NeoMundi observation that measured it, by its request_id tag.
Compare two runs only when their measurement_version matches, as you already do for model versions.
Find out, for free, which of your traced calls could be measured, with submit=False.

entrypoint.snippet:
mlflow.openai.autolog()
processor = NeoMundiMlflowProcessor(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io").install()
client.chat.completions.create(model=..., messages=...)
processor.flush()

refusals: A count written by anything but MLflow's openai autolog -- the Agents SDK tracer's zero fill, LiteLLM's estimate, LangChain's usage_metadata, a hand-written span -- is never submitted.
No provider usage, a partial one or a zero total; never estimated, never rebuilt.
Agent, chain, workflow and task spans are sums of calls already measured; tools, retrievers and embeddings are not model calls.
The measurement API is unreachable, so the failure is reported and your call is untouched.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. One observation per measured model call; aggregate spans are never billed. Start with submit=False, which needs no key and opens no socket.

integrations.name: OpenAI Agents SDK

technology.name: OpenAI Agents SDK
technology.what_it_is: OpenAI's framework for agentic applications: agents with tools, handoffs, guardrails and sessions, run in a loop by a Runner, with built-in tracing and pluggable trace processors.

evidence.reason: Four model calls of a real Agent run through the real Runner on OpenAIResponsesModel, against Ollama's OpenAI-compatible /v1/responses endpoint, whose usage block publishes integer token counts. Two plain runs plus a tool run that produced two model calls -- the tool-call blind spot, closed on a real run. Two further phases were refused on real spans and billed nothing: a Chat Completions generation span (unverified token count) and a run with trace_include_sensitive_data=False (no provider response on the span). Served measurement_version 3.5.0 on all four.

routes_verified: LitellmModel (refused) -- litellm 1.111.0, estimate observed on a silent provider
AnyLLMModel (refused while loaded) -- any-llm-sdk 1.55.0, source read, not run

value.host_keeps: The Agents SDK keeps the agent loop, tools, handoffs, guardrails and its tracing -- including its own exporter to the OpenAI dashboard and any processor you registered. The processor is appended and evicts nobody.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of every model call the agent loop makes -- the call that decides on a tool and the one that reads its result -- with the provider's own token count and the latency the SDK recorded, each outcome naming the agent and the tools it requested.
complements_not_replaces: the Agents SDK's tracing and the OpenAI traces dashboard
typical_use: Measure each step of a tool-using agent, not only its final answer.
Detect a behavioural regression that appears only when the model decides on, or reads, a tool.
Find out, for free, which of your agents' calls could be measured, with submit=False.

entrypoint.snippet:
processor = NeoMundiTraceProcessor(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io").install()
result = await Runner.run(agent, "What is the weather in Paris?")
processor.flush()

refusals: A Chat Completions or LiteLLM generation span is never submitted; its usage is zero-filled, or a local estimate, and cannot be traced to the provider.
Turn and task spans are sums of calls already measured; tool executions and agent steps are not model calls.
No provider usage, a partial one, a run without sensitive data, or AnyLLMModel loaded -- the count's origin cannot be established.
The measurement API is unreachable, so the failure is reported and your agent run is untouched.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. An agent run is billed once per model call, so a tool-using run costs several observations. Start with submit=False, which needs no key and opens no socket.

integrations.name: OpenTelemetry

technology.name: OpenTelemetry (GenAI semantic conventions)
technology.what_it_is: The vendor-neutral tracing standard. Instrumentations for model clients (contrib openai-v2, OpenLLMetry and others) emit GenAI spans that the application exports to the backend it already runs.

evidence.reason: Four real interactions through the openai client instrumented by opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai-v2, against Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint, with NeoMundiSpanProcessor on the tracer provider. The application declares the count from reply.usage.total_tokens; all four served measurement_version 3.5.0 and were re-read as persisted. Two further phases were refused on real spans and billed nothing: a span carrying the provider's usage where the application declared nothing, and a streamed call without include_usage. OpenTelemetry has no attribute distinguishing a published count from an estimate, so a count the application does not declare is refused rather than read off the span.

value.host_keeps: OpenTelemetry keeps the instrumentation, the pipeline, the exporters, the sampling and the tracing backend you already run. The processor is added next to your exporters and replaces nothing.
value.neomundi_adds: Signed, independently verifiable behavioural measurement of a model call you already trace, using the latency the trace observed -- and the NeoMundi request_id written into the same trace. It never turns a span's token count into a measurement: a span cannot prove where that count came from.
complements_not_replaces: your tracing backend (Jaeger, Tempo, Honeycomb, Datadog...)
typical_use: Measure the model calls of an application that is already traced, without a second timer or a second instrumentation.
Jump from a trace in your backend to its NeoMundi observation, and back, with neomundi.request_id.
Find out, for free, which of your traced calls could be measured, with submit=False.

entrypoint.snippet:
processor = NeoMundiSpanProcessor(api_key=..., base_url="https://api.neomundi.io")
tracer_provider.add_span_processor(processor)
with processor.interaction() as interaction:
    reply = client.chat.completions.create(model=..., messages=...)
    interaction.declare(token_count=reply.usage.total_tokens if reply.usage else None)

refusals: A token count read from a span is never submitted; only the count the caller declares from its provider's response.
No GenAI span, or more than one, inside an interaction -- which call is meant is not guessed.
A failed model call, or an exception in the application's block, is not measured.
The measurement API is unreachable, so the failure is reported and your call is untouched.

billing.note: Every submitted observation is a billed measurement; there is no trace-only route. Nothing is billed for a span alone: only an interaction with a declared count is submitted. Start with submit=False, which needs no key and opens no socket.
